hrv_sdnn.label: Heart rate variability (SDNN)
hrv_sdnn.basis: product threshold: 10% of the earlier median; HRV varies widely between people, so only your own trend is used

hrv_rmssd.label: Heart rate variability (RMSSD)
hrv_rmssd.basis: product threshold: 10%. RMSSD is a different method from SDNN and is never combined with it

vo2max.label: Cardio fitness (estimated VO₂ max)
vo2max.basis: product threshold: 1 mL/kg/min. Watch estimates can be off by more than this for an individual; the direction over months matters more than any one change

sleep_hours.label: Sleep duration
sleep_hours.basis: 20 minutes, measured as distance from 7–9 hours (adult consensus: 7 hours or more)

walking_speed.label: Walking speed
walking_speed.basis: 0.05 m/s, a small meaningful change in older adults (Perera et al., 2006)

weight.label: Body weight
weight.basis: product threshold: 1.5% of body weight; direction only counts when weight is one of your goals

systolic.label: Systolic blood pressure
systolic.basis: product threshold: 5 mmHg in averaged home readings; targets come from your clinician

diastolic.label: Diastolic blood pressure
diastolic.basis: product threshold: 3 mmHg in averaged home readings; targets come from your clinician

hba1c.label: HbA1c
hba1c.basis: product threshold: 0.3 percentage points between lab results; lab-to-lab variation exists, so discuss with your clinician

cardio_fitness.label: Cardio fitness
cardio_fitness.definition: Improve aerobic fitness, judged by the direction of estimated VO₂ max and heart rate at the same effort over months.
cardio_fitness.needs_external: Optional: a laboratory exercise test, if your clinician thinks it is useful.
options: Build toward 150–300 minutes of moderate activity a week, adding vigorous sessions gradually (US Physical Activity Guidelines).
Repeat a familiar route so comparisons are like for like.
questions: Is there any reason I should not increase my exercise intensity?
Would an exercise test add anything for me?
cardio_fitness.guardrail: The watch estimate is not a laboratory measurement and cannot clear you for vigorous exercise.

weight_management.label: Weight management
weight_management.definition: Move body weight in the direction you and your clinician agree on, judged by weekly averages.
weight_management.needs_external: A scale, or regular entries. The watch does not measure weight.
weight_management.period: Monthly direction of weekly averages; daily weight swings by a kilogram or more.
options: Combine activity with eating changes; activity alone usually moves weight slowly.
Weigh at the same time of day.
questions: What weight change would be meaningful for my health?
Are any of my medicines affecting my weight?
weight_management.guardrail: Calories burned are estimates; the product never converts them into predicted weight loss.

blood_pressure.label: Blood-pressure management
blood_pressure.definition: Keep averaged home blood pressure within the target your clinician sets.
blood_pressure.needs_external: A validated upper-arm cuff (see validatebp.org), used with good technique. The watch does not measure blood pressure values.
blood_pressure.period: Weekly averages; your clinician decides on changes.
options: Measure seated after 5 minutes of rest, arm supported, twice, morning and evening, for a week before a visit.
Follow the activity plan your clinician set.
questions: What is my target, and what should I do if my averages are above it?
Should I bring my cuff to check it against yours?
blood_pressure.guardrail: No medication advice. The product never suggests starting, stopping or changing a medicine.

glucose.label: Glucose-related goals
glucose.definition: Work with your clinician on HbA1c and glucose; use activity as one supporting behavior.
measures: Glucose sensor, if prescribed or worn
glucose.needs_external: Periodic HbA1c lab results. The watch cannot measure HbA1c or glucose.
glucose.period: HbA1c reflects about three months; results are usually months apart.
options: A recognized lifestyle-change program (such as the National Diabetes Prevention Program) for people with prediabetes.
Regular activity spread across the week.
questions: When should my HbA1c be checked again?
Would a lifestyle-change program be covered for me?
glucose.guardrail: No claim that the watch measures or predicts glucose, and no medication advice.

sleep_consistency.label: Sleep consistency
sleep_consistency.definition: Sleep 7 hours or more on a regular schedule.
sleep_consistency.needs_external: Your own notes on how rested you feel.
options: Keep a regular wake time, including weekends.
questions: Could snoring, insomnia or a medicine be affecting my sleep?
sleep_consistency.guardrail: Sleep estimates cannot diagnose a sleep disorder.

mobility.label: Mobility
mobility.definition: Keep walking speed and steadiness so you can walk independently.
mobility.needs_external: A clinician's gait or balance assessment if things change.
mobility.period: Every 3–6 months against your own last year.
options: Strength and balance exercise (the US guidelines recommend it for older adults).
questions: Would a balance or strength assessment help me?
Is anything I take affecting my balance?
mobility.guardrail: No fall-risk prediction for an individual.

activity_adherence.label: Activity adherence
activity_adherence.definition: Reach 150 minutes of brisk-or-harder activity in most weeks.
options: Short bouts count; spread activity across the week.
questions: Is there any activity I should avoid?
activity_adherence.guardrail: Rings and streaks reward effort; they say nothing about safety.

mental_wellbeing.label: Mental well-being
mental_wellbeing.definition: Notice patterns in mood alongside sleep and activity.
mental_wellbeing.needs_external: Your own mood logs and validated questionnaires. Not collected in this demo.
options: Talk to someone. In the US, call or text 988 if you are in crisis.
questions: Would a screening questionnaire be useful for me?
mental_wellbeing.guardrail: Mood is never inferred from heart rate or sleep.

references.name: FRIEND registry (Fitness Registry and the Importance of Exercise National Database)
references.what: Laboratory cardiopulmonary exercise tests, by age and sex, treadmill and cycle reported separately.
references.match: Method mismatch: the watch estimates VO₂ max from heart rate and movement; FRIEND measures it with a gas analyzer. Comparing the two needs a stated correction or a caveat.
references.cite: Kaminsky et al., Mayo Clinic Proceedings, 2022

references.name: Normal walking speed: a descriptive meta-analysis
references.what: Comfortable gait speed measured over short courses, by age decade and sex.
references.match: Method mismatch: course-measured speed versus the phone's passive estimate during everyday walking.

references.name: Step-count activity categories
references.what: Graduated categories from under 5,000 to 10,000 or more steps a day.
references.match: Used here only to name activity levels, not as a health benchmark.

references.name: National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES)
references.what: Standardized, examiner-measured blood pressure in a nationally representative US sample.
references.match: Method mismatch: examiner-measured office readings versus home cuff readings.
references.cite: CDC National Center for Health Statistics

cohorts.label: Illustrative synthetic cohort: generated for this demo from a documented seed (9090). Not a published reference.

urgent_guidance: Call emergency services (911 in the US) now. Symptoms like these need immediate care whatever the watch shows; a normal-looking chart is not reassurance.
